landing.pricing.faq.renew.question: Do subscriptions renew automatically?
landing.pricing.faq.renew.answer: Yes. Monthly and yearly subscriptions renew at the end of each billing period. You can cancel anytime from Settings → Billing and keep access until the current period ends.
landing.pricing.faq.upgrade.question: What happens to my credits when I upgrade?
landing.pricing.faq.upgrade.answer: The upgrade takes effect right away, and the price is prorated by the time left in your current billing period. Extra credits for the new plan are prorated by the same proportion (never below zero). Credits already in your account are kept.
landing.pricing.faq.scheduled.question: How do credits work for a downgrade or a change at period end?
landing.pricing.faq.scheduled.answer: Changes that take effect at the end of the period, such as downgrades, aren't charged or refunded now. Your current plan's credits stay usable until the period ends, and unused credits don't roll over. Once the new plan starts, you get its full credits.
landing.pricing.faq.expiry.question: When do my credits expire?
landing.pricing.faq.expiry.answer: Monthly plan credits are valid for one month. Yearly plan credits and one-time credit packs are valid for one year. You can see the exact expiration date for every credit grant on your Credits page.
landing.pricing.faq.pack.question: Do I need a subscription to buy a credit pack?
landing.pricing.faq.pack.answer: No. Credit packs are one-time purchases with no automatic renewal. You can use one on its own or add it to an account that already has a subscription.
landing.pricing.faq.cost.question: How many credits does an image cost?
landing.pricing.faq.cost.answer: The cost depends on the model and the number of images you request. The exact credit cost is shown before you generate, so you can switch models or adjust the quantity first.
landing.pricing.faq.fail.question: Will I be charged for a failed generation?
landing.pricing.faq.fail.answer: No. Credits are charged for completed results. If a generation fails before producing a result, the reserved credits are returned to your balance automatically.
landing.pricing.faq.invoice.question: Where can I find payment records and invoices?
landing.pricing.faq.invoice.answer: Open Settings → Payments to review completed orders. When the payment provider supplies an invoice link, it appears alongside the corresponding payment.
landing.pricing.faq.refund.question: Can I request a refund?
landing.pricing.faq.refund.answer: Paid services are billed in advance. Refund requests are reviewed case by case under the Terms of Service; contact support with your order number so the payment can be checked.

landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

landing.home.faq.faq_1.question: What is an AI video generator?
landing.home.faq.faq_1.answer: It is a tool that turns a written description or reference into video. You type what you want to see, pick a model, duration and resolution, and the video is rendered for you in seconds — no camera, no stock library, no editor.
landing.home.faq.faq_2.question: Is it free to use?
landing.home.faq.faq_2.answer: There is a free tier. Sign up and you get welcome credits, which is enough for a good handful of images, with no payment details required. Paid plans add the higher-fidelity models, more monthly credits and API access.
landing.home.faq.faq_3.question: Which models can I use?
landing.home.faq.faq_3.answer: Use FLUX.2 for fast drafts, Nano Banana Pro for difficult detail, GPT Image 2 for prompt-faithful layouts, and Seedream 5.0 Pro for production visuals and multi-reference work. You can switch between them in the same prompt box.
landing.home.faq.faq_4.question: Can it render text inside images?
landing.home.faq.faq_4.answer: Yes. Put the exact words in quotes in your prompt — a headline on a poster, the wording on a product label — and they are rendered as part of the image. Nano Banana Pro and GPT Image 2 are the strongest choices when the text has to be perfect.
landing.home.faq.faq_5.question: How do credits work?
landing.home.faq.faq_5.answer: Each render costs credits based on the model and how many images you asked for, from 12 credits for GPT Image 2. The cost is shown next to the generate button before you commit, and your balance replaces it once you are signed in.
landing.home.faq.faq_6.question: Do I need to install anything or bring an API key?
landing.home.faq.faq_6.answer: Neither. The models run on our side, so there is nothing to download, no GPU required and no key to paste. It works from any laptop or phone browser.

landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_1.question: What is a text-to-video generator?
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_1.answer: A text-to-video generator is an AI tool that creates a new video from a written prompt. You describe the subject and visual direction, and the model renders a video that follows those instructions.
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_2.question: How do I create an AI video from text?
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_2.answer: Enter a prompt that describes the subject, style, setting, composition, and lighting. Choose a model and aspect ratio, then generate. You can edit the prompt and run it again to refine the result.
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_3.question: Can I use the text-to-video generator for free?
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_3.answer: Yes. New accounts receive free credits, and the credit cost is shown before each generation. Faster draft models use fewer credits than higher-detail options.
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_4.question: Can I use AI-generated videos commercially?
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_4.answer: You can use generated images for personal or commercial projects, subject to the terms of the selected model provider and this site's terms of service. Review both before publishing paid work.
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_5.question: How do I write good text-to-video prompts?
landing.text_to_image.faq.faq_5.answer: Start with the main subject, then add the setting, style, composition, lighting, color palette, and important details. Put exact wording in quotation marks when the image needs visible text.

landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_1.questio: What is an image to video generator?
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_1.answer: An image to video generator starts from an existing image and a text prompt. The model uses the reference image as visual grounding or first frame, then renders motion based on your edit instructions.
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_2.questio: How similar will the result be to my reference?
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_2.answer: Similarity depends on the prompt. Ask the model to preserve identity, pose, framing, lighting, or materials when those details matter, and only describe the change you want.
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_3.questio: Can I use the image to video generator for free?
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_3.answer: Yes. New accounts receive free credits. Each generation shows its credit cost before you run it.
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_4.answer: Uploads and generated results stay in your private library. They are not shown publicly on this site.
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_5.questio: How do I write a good image editing prompt?
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_5.answer: Describe the change directly, then list important details to preserve. For example: “remove the bicycle, rebuild the garden naturally, and keep the bench, camera angle, lighting, and shadows unchanged.”
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_6.questio: Which image formats and reference limits are supported?
landing.image_to_image.faq.faq_6.answer: You can upload JPG, PNG, or WebP images up to 5MB each. Available models support multiple references, and the uploader follows the selected model’s limit.

Both. Quote short copy for posters and labels; lean on it for engraving, crowded stalls and macro surfaces when other models smear the details.

It uses Nano Banana Pro from 36 credits per successful image. A failed run costs nothing.
What happens to the image I upload?
It stays private to your account and is stored only so the model can process it and the result can remain in your library.
How is AI style transfer different from a photo filter?
A filter mainly changes colour and contrast. AI style transfer redraws textures, shapes, edges, and materials while using the original subject and composition as a guide.
Can style transfer preserve a person's face?
It aims to keep identity, pose, and framing recognizable, but stronger styles can alter small facial details. Use a sharp, front-facing source when likeness matters most.

The agent saves each project's URL and key in a private local credentials file (readable only by you), never in a repository. admin.agent.skill_prompt:
Please add "{app}" ({url}) as a ShipAny project you can manage, under the project name "{name}".

1. If you don't have the shipany-admin skill yet, download these two files into a shipany-admin folder in your skills directory (e.g. ~/.claude/skills/shipany-admin/). If it's already installed, skip this step and don't overwrite it: the client can read every project's key, so update it only when I explicitly ask, from a site I trust.
   - {url}/api/admin/agent/skill?file=SKILL.md → shipany-admin/SKILL.md
   - {url}/api/admin/agent/skill?file=admin-client.mjs → shipany-admin/scripts/admin-client.mjs
2. I'll send you this project's admin key (starts with sa_admin_) next. Save it via stdin — never as a command argument — and never repeat it afterwards:
   printf '%s' '<key>' | node <skill-dir>/scripts/admin-client.mjs add {name} {url}
3. Run node <skill-dir>/scripts/admin-client.mjs --project {name} list and tell me which operations you can call.
4. From then on, follow SKILL.md strictly for the admin tasks I give you; when managing several projects, name the project with --project on every call.
admin.agent.full_docs: Full reference (idempotency, audit, local stdio MCP bridge, CLI agent/key management): docs/admin-agent.md in the repository.
admin.agent.never_warning: A non-expiring key works until you revoke it. Give the agent minimal roles, and revoke the key as soon as it's no longer needed or may have leaked.
admin.agent.created_warning: Copy this key now — it won't be shown again. Store it in the agent's secret store, never in the repository.
admin.agent.revoke_warning: Revoke this key? Agents using it lose access immediately. This can't be undone.
admin.agent.accounts_hint: Each agent is an API-type user: its permissions are the RBAC roles you assign, and it signs in only with its admin API keys. Agents aren't counted as users.
admin.agent.agent_form_hint: Pick the roles this agent acts with. You can only grant roles whose permissions you hold yourself.
